candidates.title: Maus
candidates.rationale: Its visual metaphors, difficult father–son relationship and layered testimony make it the strongest overall synthesis of formal achievement, historical force and sustained critical recognition.

candidates.title: Watchmen
candidates.creators_reported: Alan Moore; Dave Gibbons; John Higgins
candidates.rationale: A densely constructed examination of power and moral compromise, using page design, recurring images and parallel narratives with extraordinary control.

candidates.title: Calvin and Hobbes
candidates.rationale: Combines visual invention, comic timing and emotional intelligence with unusual consistency across a complete, deliberately bounded run.

candidates.title: Krazy Kat
candidates.rationale: Its changing landscapes, elastic language and endlessly varied love triangle make it one of comics' foundational works of poetic modernism.

candidates.title: The Sandman
candidates.creators_reported: Neil Gaiman; Sam Kieth, Mike Dringenberg, Jill Thompson, Marc Hempel and others
candidates.rationale: An ambitious interconnected cycle about stories, responsibility and change, balancing intimate episodes with a large mythological structure.

candidates.title: Peanuts
candidates.rationale: Turns economical drawing and repeated situations into a remarkably durable language for loneliness, failure, affection and hope.

candidates.title: Akira
candidates.rationale: Its spectacular architecture, spatial clarity and escalating catastrophe transformed expectations of what long-form action comics could accomplish.

candidates.title: Persepolis
candidates.scope: Complete memoir, including the European years.
candidates.rationale: A forceful personal account whose stark images connect political upheaval to the contradictory experience of growing up.

candidates.title: Fun Home
candidates.rationale: Its recursive structure and interplay of documentary detail, literature and images produce an exceptionally rich investigation of memory and family identity.

candidates.title: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind
candidates.manga_context: Crossover; not a standard demographic magazine
candidates.rationale: A morally searching ecological epic whose political complexity and visual world-building extend far beyond its animated adaptation.

candidates.title: Jimmy Corrigan, the Smartest Kid on Earth
candidates.rationale: Exquisitely controlled page architecture turns ordinary embarrassment and inherited loneliness into a multigenerational tragedy.

candidates.title: From Hell
candidates.scope: Complete original narrative and its appendices.
candidates.rationale: Its densely imagined Victorian world and abrasive visual atmosphere make a murder investigation into an inquiry into class, violence and history.

candidates.title: Little Nemo in Slumberland
candidates.rationale: A landmark of page-scale invention: architecture, colour, metamorphosis and dream logic become the engines of storytelling.

candidates.title: Locas (Love and Rockets)
candidates.scope: Maggie, Hopey and connected Locas stories; excludes Palomar.
candidates.rationale: Its characters age, change and accumulate history with a depth that rewards decades of serial storytelling.

candidates.title: Palomar (Love and Rockets)
candidates.scope: Palomar and its connected Luba narrative; excludes Locas.
candidates.rationale: A densely populated social world whose intimate dramas, nonlinear memories and long consequences sustain an extraordinary communal novel.

candidates.title: Phoenix
candidates.rationale: Its movement between distant past and future gives comics an unusually expansive treatment of mortality, civilisation and recurrence.

candidates.title: The Adventures of Tintin
candidates.scope: Completed Hergé albums; not later continuations.
candidates.rationale: Exceptionally clear visual storytelling and intricate adventure construction underpin its historical stature; the early colonial caricatures also require critical scrutiny.

candidates.title: Bone
candidates.rationale: A rare fusion of expressive cartoon comedy and sustained epic adventure, with accessible storytelling that remains rewarding for adults.

candidates.title: Building Stories
candidates.rationale: Its physically separate pieces let readers assemble lives and memories, making the material form of the work part of its meaning.

candidates.title: The Dark Knight Returns
candidates.creators_reported: Frank Miller; Klaus Janson; Lynn Varley
candidates.rationale: Aggressive layouts and a combustible public world helped redefine the superhero graphic novel, although its politics remain a source of disagreement.

candidates.title: Asterios Polyp
candidates.rationale: Colour, lettering, drawing style and page composition express conflicting ways of seeing rather than merely illustrating the dialogue.

candidates.title: Pogo
candidates.rationale: Linguistic play, ensemble comedy and political bite make its swamp community one of the medium's richest recurring settings.

candidates.title: The Incal
candidates.rationale: Mœbius's visual imagination gives a sprawling spiritual adventure an influence far beyond its sometimes unruly plotting.

candidates.title: V for Vendetta
candidates.rationale: A demanding exploration of authoritarianism, freedom and the ethics of resistance, distinguished by its controlled visual atmosphere.

candidates.title: The Eternaut
candidates.creators_reported: Héctor Germán Oesterheld; Francisco Solano López
candidates.rationale: Its collective protagonist and recognisable Buenos Aires setting turn an invasion story into an enduring statement about solidarity.

candidates.title: Black Hole
candidates.rationale: Meticulous black-and-white imagery makes adolescent dread, desire and exclusion physically disturbing and emotionally persuasive.

candidates.title: Berserk
candidates.scope: Miura-authored narrative through 2021; continuation treated separately.
candidates.rationale: Extraordinary draftsmanship and a powerful account of trauma and attachment outweigh significant unevenness and an incomplete authorial ending.

candidates.title: The Arrival
candidates.rationale: Its invented world makes unfamiliarity tangible, communicating migration and belonging through images with remarkable clarity and empathy.

candidates.title: Corto Maltese
candidates.rationale: Sparse drawing, suggestive dialogue and historical ambiguity make adventure feel dreamlike, worldly and melancholy.

candidates.title: One Piece
candidates.scope: Main manga; rank applies to published work, not an assumed ending.
candidates.rationale: Its exuberant world-building and long-range emotional payoffs give popular adventure an unusual scale and imaginative coherence.

candidates.title: Astérix (Goscinny–Uderzo albums)
candidates.rationale: Verbal wit, expressive physical comedy and tightly organised adventures make its finest albums models of comic construction.

candidates.title: All-Star Superman
candidates.creators_reported: Grant Morrison; Frank Quitely; Jamie Grant
candidates.rationale: Condenses decades of superhero mythology into a generous, emotionally direct story about power, kindness and legacy.

candidates.title: Saga of the Swamp Thing (Alan Moore run)
candidates.creators_reported: Alan Moore; Stephen Bissette; John Totleben; Rick Veitch and others
candidates.scope: Moore's issues #20–64 and associated Annual #2 material.
candidates.rationale: Transforms a horror property through lyrical narration, ecological imagination and an unusually moving account of identity.

candidates.title: Lone Wolf and Cub
candidates.rationale: Kojima's brushwork and sustained attention to movement give a revenge epic exceptional visual power and tragic gravity.

candidates.title: Donald Duck and Uncle Scrooge (Carl Barks stories)
candidates.scope: Barks's duck stories; Don Rosa's later work is a separate entry.
candidates.rationale: Combines beautifully lucid cartooning with character-driven comedy and adventures whose social observations exceed their family-entertainment packaging.

candidates.title: Monster
candidates.rationale: Patient characterisation and a carefully sustained moral dilemma give this European-set thriller unusual human weight.

candidates.title: The Rose of Versailles
candidates.scope: Original core story; later supplementary episodes excluded.
candidates.rationale: A defining achievement of historical shōjo, joining political upheaval to questions of gender, desire and social position.

candidates.title: Berlin
candidates.rationale: Dense social observation and lucid visual staging chart a city's everyday life under gathering political catastrophe.

candidates.title: Epileptic
candidates.scope: Complete L'Ascension du Haut Mal narrative.
candidates.rationale: Its symbolic imagery turns family illness into a visual world of fear, fantasy, conflict and attempted escape.

candidates.title: Here
candidates.rationale: The overlapping histories of a single place become a radically different way of organising narrative time.

candidates.title: Slam Dunk
candidates.rationale: Its growing command of bodies in motion and team psychology culminates in some of comics' most accomplished sports storytelling.

candidates.title: A Contract with God
candidates.rationale: A major milestone in the modern graphic novel, using theatrical gesture and environmental detail to explore ordinary lives and moral disappointment.

candidates.title: Safe Area Goražde
candidates.rationale: Immersive reporting and crowded, particular images preserve civilian experience without pretending that a reporter is an invisible observer.

candidates.title: Daytripper
candidates.rationale: Its recurring encounters with mortality give everyday attachments a cumulative emotional force while exploiting serial structure.

candidates.title: Blankets
candidates.rationale: Fluid, lyrical cartooning joins remembered intimacy to the difficult separation of personal identity from inherited belief.

candidates.title: My Favorite Thing Is Monsters
candidates.genres: Mystery; coming of age; art; LGBTQ+
candidates.rationale: Notebook imagery becomes an expansive visual language for outsiderhood, desire and historical memory; the first book supplies the strongest established reception.

candidates.title: Dragon Ball
candidates.scope: Original 42-volume manga; excludes Dragon Ball Super.
candidates.rationale: Toriyama's clarity, comic timing and kinetic drawing established an extraordinarily influential grammar for action manga.

candidates.title: Hellboy (Mignola cycle)
candidates.creators_reported: Mike Mignola; Duncan Fegredo and collaborators
candidates.scope: Core Hellboy narrative through Hellboy in Hell; wider universe excluded.
candidates.rationale: Bold design and folklore-rich atmosphere make its monsters, silences and fatalism immediately distinctive.

candidates.title: Saga
candidates.scope: Main series as published; no credit for an unwritten conclusion.
candidates.rationale: Inventive visual design and an emotionally legible family story sustain its broad appeal, with incompleteness limiting certainty about its final standing.

candidates.title: Understanding Comics
candidates.rationale: A landmark argument delivered through the medium it explains, making its conceptual ideas inseparable from its own visual demonstrations.

candidates.title: Batman: Year One
candidates.creators_reported: Frank Miller; David Mazzucchelli; Richmond Lewis
candidates.rationale: Restrained images and parallel character arcs give a familiar origin the precision and atmosphere of a compact crime novel.

candidates.title: MAD (Harvey Kurtzman's comic-book run)
candidates.creators_reported: Harvey Kurtzman; Will Elder; Wally Wood; Jack Davis; John Severin
candidates.rationale: Its ruthless parodies and densely timed visual jokes changed the way popular culture could mock its own conventions.

candidates.title: Barefoot Gen
candidates.rationale: Its blunt immediacy and survivor's perspective make the destruction of Hiroshima and its aftermath impossible to reduce to abstraction.

candidates.title: 20th Century Boys
candidates.scope: Includes the concluding 21st Century Boys volumes.
candidates.rationale: Childhood memory becomes the structure of a large-scale conspiracy thriller, carried by Urasawa's expressive character drawing.

candidates.title: Fullmetal Alchemist
candidates.rationale: Balances humour, political consequence and a large cast within one of mainstream manga's most satisfyingly resolved long narratives.

candidates.title: Ghost World
candidates.scope: Collected Eightball story; not the whole anthology.
candidates.rationale: Its economical dialogue and uneasy spaces capture the cruelty, tenderness and uncertainty of a friendship at a turning point.

candidates.title: Fantastic Four (Lee–Kirby run)
candidates.creators_reported: Stan Lee; Jack Kirby; Joe Sinnott and collaborators
candidates.scope: Lee–Kirby era, centred on #1–102 and its annuals.
candidates.rationale: An extraordinary sustained burst of character and world creation, with Kirby's expanding visual imagination at its centre.

candidates.title: The Obscure Cities
candidates.scope: Main cycle; The Leaning Girl is included here, not separately ranked.
candidates.rationale: Architecture functions as narrative logic, producing haunting societies whose designs embody their intellectual and political assumptions.

candidates.title: Amazing Spider-Man (Lee–Ditko run)
candidates.scope: Amazing Fantasy #15 and Amazing Spider-Man #1–38, plus their original annuals.
candidates.rationale: Its fusion of personal frustration, moral responsibility and distinctive action staging fundamentally reshaped the superhero protagonist.

candidates.title: The Life and Times of Scrooge McDuck
candidates.rationale: Builds an unexpectedly moving character biography from adventure continuity, meticulous visual detail and the cost of ambition.

candidates.title: Daredevil: Born Again
candidates.rationale: A remarkably concentrated fall-and-recovery narrative, with expressive visual storytelling and unusually strong control of pace.

candidates.title: The Spirit (Eisner newspaper stories)
candidates.scope: Eisner-led classic stories, with emphasis on the postwar period.
candidates.rationale: Its inventive openings, expressive cityscapes and compact human dramas expanded the possibilities of short comics.

candidates.title: It Was the War of the Trenches
candidates.rationale: Bleak, cumulative episodes strip military mythology away from the bodily experience and arbitrary violence of trench warfare.

candidates.title: March
candidates.creators_reported: John Lewis; Andrew Aydin; Nate Powell
candidates.rationale: Connects public history to participant testimony with urgent pacing and expressive visual treatment of collective action.

candidates.title: Mushishi
candidates.rationale: Its quiet, morally ambiguous encounters resist simple victories and find beauty in the uneasy coexistence of human and nonhuman life.

candidates.title: Vagabond
candidates.rationale: Exceptional brushwork and bodily presence gradually turn a sword-fighting epic toward questions of violence, labour and self-knowledge.

candidates.title: Yokohama Kaidashi Kikō
candidates.genres: Quiet science fiction; everyday life; nature
candidates.rationale: Creates a distinctive emotional register through landscape, pauses and the gentle observation of a world undergoing irreversible change.

candidates.title: Nana
candidates.rationale: Its fashionable surface conceals unusually perceptive treatment of dependency, ambition and the instability of young adult relationships.

candidates.title: Uzumaki
candidates.rationale: A simple visual motif grows into an astonishing succession of unsettling transformations and an enveloping atmosphere of obsession.

candidates.title: The Heart of Thomas
candidates.rationale: An emotionally intricate school story whose page rhythms and interiority helped enlarge the expressive possibilities of shōjo manga.

candidates.title: The Art of Charlie Chan Hock Chye
candidates.rationale: Its invented artistic biography makes changing comics styles a means of questioning the construction of national history.

candidates.title: Grass
candidates.rationale: Combines witness testimony with stark, expansive drawing to convey both historical atrocity and the long life of its consequences.

candidates.title: Mafalda
candidates.rationale: A child's questions expose the absurdities of adult politics, inequality and convention with remarkable economy.

candidates.title: Uncanny X-Men (Claremont's first run)
candidates.creators_reported: Chris Claremont; Dave Cockrum; John Byrne; Paul Smith; John Romita Jr.; Marc Silvestri and others
candidates.scope: Claremont's first principal run; Dark Phoenix and Days of Future Past are included here.
candidates.rationale: Long emotional arcs and a richly differentiated ensemble make its best stretches landmarks of serial superhero storytelling.

candidates.title: Yotsuba&!
candidates.rationale: Its finely observed gestures and visual timing turn ordinary discoveries into an unusually generous and sustained comedy of attention.

candidates.title: A Drifting Life
candidates.rationale: An expansive account of artistic formation that places the emergence of gekiga within everyday work, family and cultural change.

candidates.title: Fruits Basket
candidates.rationale: A seemingly light premise develops into a compassionate, carefully interconnected treatment of abuse, belonging and emotional recovery.

candidates.title: The Poe Clan
candidates.scope: Classic original cycle, with later revival identified separately.
candidates.rationale: Its shifting chronology and lyrical pages make supernatural longevity a vehicle for grief, desire and exclusion.

candidates.title: Pluto
candidates.creators_reported: Naoki Urasawa; Takashi Nagasaki; based on Osamu Tezuka
candidates.rationale: Reworks an Astro Boy story into a tightly focused inquiry into memory, personhood and the moral afterlife of war.

candidates.title: Prince Valiant (Hal Foster)
candidates.rationale: Grand visual composition and sustained historical adventure give the Sunday page the scope of an illustrated epic.

candidates.title: Town of Evening Calm, Country of Cherry Blossoms
candidates.genres: Historical fiction; family; aftermath of war
candidates.rationale: Its understated domestic detail reveals how a historical catastrophe persists across generations without relying on constant spectacle.

candidates.title: Onward Towards Our Noble Deaths
candidates.rationale: Mizuki's contrast between cartoon figures and dense environments gives military absurdity and expendable human life a devastating force.

candidates.title: Buddha
candidates.scope: Complete original series; a fictionalised life, not a historical biography.
candidates.rationale: Tezuka's broad narrative range and humanistic concerns create an ambitious popular epic about suffering and moral transformation.

candidates.title: Astro Boy
candidates.rationale: Its combination of accessible adventure and questions about technological power and personhood remains central to manga's development.

candidates.title: Goodnight Punpun
candidates.rationale: Its clash of photographic environments and symbolic character design creates a distinctive, often punishing account of damaged adulthood.

candidates.title: Palestine
candidates.rationale: A foundational work of comics reportage, attentive to individual voices, physical environments and the reporter's own position.

candidates.title: Footnotes in Gaza
candidates.rationale: Patiently reconstructs contested historical events through interviews while making uncertainty and the labour of reporting visible.

candidates.title: The Photographer
candidates.creators_reported: Emmanuel Guibert; Didier Lefèvre; Frédéric Lemercier
candidates.rationale: Its integration of photographs and drawn sequences creates a distinctive record of travel, observation and medical work.

candidates.title: Stuck Rubber Baby
candidates.rationale: Dense cartooning supports an emotionally and politically complex account of coming out amid struggles over racial justice.

candidates.title: American Splendor
candidates.creators_reported: Harvey Pekar; Robert Crumb and numerous artists
candidates.rationale: Makes ordinary speech, work and social friction into compelling comics while preserving the different voices of its collaborating artists.

candidates.title: The Tale of One Bad Rat
candidates.rationale: Clear, compassionate storytelling links personal survival with landscape, art and the gradual rebuilding of trust.

candidates.title: American Born Chinese
candidates.rationale: Its interlocking narratives use the relationship between caricature and identity with unusual structural purpose.

candidates.title: The Arab of the Future
candidates.rationale: The child's limited viewpoint and sharply observed domestic scenes complicate easy judgments about culture, authority and family.

candidates.title: Aya of Yop City
candidates.rationale: Its lively ensemble and social specificity offer a richly ordinary view of urban African life, driven by excellent character comedy.

candidates.title: Alack Sinner
candidates.rationale: Radical black-and-white design turns detective fiction toward exile, memory and the contradictions of urban life.

candidates.title: Mort Cinder
candidates.rationale: Breccia's expressive textures give its journeys through history an uncanny intensity and a persistent human cost.

candidates.title: Perramus
candidates.rationale: Its unstable visual world and dark humour transform dictatorship, erasure and memory into a singularly inventive adventure.

candidates.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Steel Ball Run
candidates.scope: Part 7 only; the whole JoJo franchise is not separately ranked.
candidates.rationale: Its long race structure, eccentric visual imagination and developing partnerships make it a particularly accomplished self-contained JoJo cycle.

candidates.title: Ōoku: The Inner Chambers
candidates.rationale: Its historical reimagining develops into a sophisticated inquiry into institutions, gendered power and the management of public knowledge.

candidates.title: Two-Fisted Tales (Kurtzman era)
candidates.creators_reported: Harvey Kurtzman; John Severin; Wally Wood; Jack Davis and collaborators
candidates.scope: Kurtzman's original Two-Fisted Tales work; later editorial eras excluded. References mainly establish its creator/history context.
candidates.rationale: Its best war stories replace uncomplicated heroism with precise staging, historical particularity and the vulnerability of individual lives.

candidates.title: The Hunting Party
candidates.scope: Original album, including editions with the later epilogue.
candidates.rationale: Atmospheric drawing and compressed political history turn an isolated gathering into a portrait of compromised power.

candidates.title: Sunny
candidates.rationale: Loose, emotionally precise drawing and shifting viewpoints produce a tender, unsentimental portrait of children living in care.

candidates.title: The Nikopol Trilogy
candidates.rationale: A distinctive painted world combines authoritarian politics, bodily unease and surreal mythology with enduring visual authority.

candidates.title: Ducks: Two Years in the Oil Sands
candidates.rationale: Detailed workplace observation connects personal experience to labour, debt, misogyny and the contradictions of resource extraction.

candidates.title: Ping Pong
candidates.rationale: Distorted perspectives and individualised movement make competitive sport a vivid study of talent, obsession and self-worth.

candidates.title: Arzach
candidates.rationale: Its compact visual inventions helped make comics fantasy stranger, more open-ended and less dependent on explanatory dialogue.

candidates.title: The Airtight Garage
candidates.rationale: An unusually influential experiment in improvisation, whose visual coherence sustains a deliberately unpredictable fictional universe.

candidates.title: Blacksad
candidates.genres: Crime noir; political history; animal allegory
candidates.rationale: Expressive character acting and lavishly controlled environments give familiar noir plots exceptional visual distinction.

candidates.title: Tekkonkinkreet
candidates.rationale: A dense, feverish city and two sharply contrasted children sustain a distinctive meditation on belonging and destructive power.

candidates.title: Blueberry (Charlier–Giraud cycle)
candidates.scope: Main Charlier–Giraud collaboration; unrelated continuations excluded.
candidates.rationale: A major achievement of serial adventure, with increasingly sophisticated landscape, action staging and a morally complicated protagonist.

candidates.title: Gaston (Franquin)
candidates.scope: Franquin's original Gaston strips and pages.
candidates.rationale: Elastic drawing and intricate mechanical disasters turn office comedy into a sustained celebration of imaginative disorder.

candidates.title: Real
candidates.rationale: Attentive character work and superb physical drawing give wheelchair basketball and difficult personal recovery exceptional dramatic weight.

candidates.title: Moomin comic strips
candidates.scope: Tove Jansson's original newspaper strips, with Lars Jansson's contributions to that period; later solo continuation excluded.
candidates.rationale: An eccentric, generous world uses comedy to unsettle ideas about respectability, work, ownership and normality.

candidates.title: Vinland Saga
candidates.rationale: Its strongest achievement is the transformation of a revenge adventure into a sustained moral inquiry about violence and constructive life.

candidates.title: The Vision (King–Walta)
candidates.creators_reported: Tom King; Gabriel Hernández Walta; Michael Walsh; Jordie Bellaire
candidates.rationale: A tightly organised suburban tragedy whose controlled images and narration turn the desire for normality into mounting dread.

candidates.title: The Far Side
candidates.rationale: Its displaced viewpoints and strange causal logic created a remarkably distinctive and influential comic language.

candidates.title: The Summit of the Gods
candidates.creators_reported: Jirō Taniguchi; based on Baku Yumemakura
candidates.rationale: Precise environments and deliberate pacing make physical endurance and the attraction of the mountain intensely tangible.

candidates.title: Doonesbury
candidates.genres: Political satire; social history; ensemble comedy
candidates.rationale: Long-term character development gives topical satire a historical memory that few other continuing strips possess.

candidates.title: Mister Miracle (King–Gerads)
candidates.rationale: Its repeated grids and disrupted perceptions bring domestic life and cosmic mythology into an unusually intimate relationship.

candidates.title: A Distant Neighborhood
candidates.rationale: A restrained return-to-childhood premise becomes a searching meditation on parenthood, regret and the limits of understanding others.

candidates.title: Popeye (E.C. Segar's Thimble Theatre)
candidates.rationale: Its eccentric cast and integration of extended adventure with physical comedy made it a foundational popular strip.

candidates.title: The Walking Man
candidates.rationale: Its commitment to small observations demonstrates how little overt plot comics need to create a deeply absorbing experience.

candidates.title: This One Summer
candidates.rationale: Its delicate handling of observation and partial understanding captures a summer in which childhood certainties begin to break down.

candidates.title: Nancy (Ernie Bushmiller)
candidates.rationale: Its apparent simplicity conceals extraordinarily exact visual engineering, making it a touchstone for the mechanics of the gag.

candidates.title: A Bride's Story
candidates.rationale: Extraordinary material detail supports a patient, humane attention to domestic labour, social obligations and relationships.

candidates.title: DC: The New Frontier
candidates.rationale: An exceptionally designed ensemble work that connects heroic idealism to the contradictions of postwar America.

candidates.title: The Kampung Boy
candidates.rationale: Warm, highly observant cartooning preserves a particular social world while making childhood experience broadly accessible.

candidates.title: In This Corner of the World
candidates.rationale: Its focus on household work, drawing and small pleasures makes wartime loss devastating without abandoning everyday life.

candidates.title: The Best We Could Do
candidates.rationale: Its shifting family perspectives connect refugee history to the difficult work of understanding parents as people.

candidates.title: The Man Without Talent
candidates.rationale: Understated absurdity and uncomfortable domestic observation turn failed schemes into an unsettling account of masculinity and withdrawal.

candidates.title: Louis Riel
candidates.rationale: Highly controlled staging and conspicuous documentation create an unusual, formally distinctive treatment of contested national history.

candidates.title: Nejishiki
candidates.scope: The individual story, not every collection carrying its title.
candidates.rationale: A compact, foundational experiment whose dream logic and imagery remain influential far beyond its length.

candidates.title: Kingdom Come
candidates.rationale: Its painted spectacle and generational argument crystallise an influential debate about superhero violence and moral responsibility.

candidates.title: Black Blizzard
candidates.rationale: An early landmark of dramatic manga, using urgent pacing and cinematic staging to pursue a more adult register of storytelling.

candidates.title: Hicksville
candidates.rationale: Uses an imagined comics culture to examine artistic memory, appropriation and the communities that make creativity possible.

candidates.title: Domu
candidates.rationale: An apartment complex becomes a brilliantly staged arena for escalating supernatural conflict and meticulously observed social space.

candidates.title: Clyde Fans
candidates.rationale: Its long rhythms and architectural spaces turn commercial decline and sibling difference into a sustained study of regret.

candidates.title: The Drifting Classroom
candidates.rationale: Its escalating terror and extreme emotional pitch helped establish the power of horror manga aimed at younger readers.

candidates.title: Marvels
candidates.rationale: Reframes a shared superhero history through ordinary human perception, with Ross's imagery restoring a sense of awe and unease.

candidates.title: Black Jack
candidates.rationale: Its episodic ethical dilemmas reveal Tezuka's ability to combine populist melodrama with persistent questions about the value of life.

candidates.title: Essex County
candidates.rationale: Loose, expressive drawing and interconnected lives give a local setting emotional and historical depth.

candidates.title: Message to Adolf
candidates.rationale: A substantial political thriller examining how ideology, secrecy and national identity entangle individual lives.

candidates.title: Hawkeye (Fraction–Aja run)
candidates.creators_reported: Matt Fraction; David Aja; Annie Wu; Javier Pulido and collaborators
candidates.rationale: Inventive visual communication and a grounded supporting cast make a superhero's everyday failures exceptionally engaging.

candidates.title: Doraemon
candidates.rationale: Its inventive gadgets and recognisable childhood failings form one of the most enduring and influential structures in family manga.

candidates.title: Blast
candidates.rationale: Its changes in visual register and troubled testimony create an unusually intense examination of self-explanation and violence.

candidates.title: Devilman
candidates.rationale: Its compressed escalation and brutal rejection of reassuring heroic resolutions gave it lasting influence on darker popular manga.

candidates.title: City of Glass (graphic adaptation)
candidates.creators_reported: Paul Karasik; David Mazzucchelli; based on Paul Auster
candidates.rationale: A model of adaptation that translates questions of language and identity into specifically visual structures.

candidates.title: Ashita no Joe
candidates.creators_reported: Asao Takamori / Ikki Kajiwara; Tetsuya Chiba
candidates.rationale: A defining sports drama whose physical struggle and social antagonism give ambition unusually tragic stakes.

candidates.title: Animal Man (Grant Morrison run)
candidates.creators_reported: Grant Morrison; Chas Truog; Doug Hazlewood and collaborators
candidates.rationale: Begins with a modest superhero family and develops into a daring examination of storytelling, suffering and authorial responsibility.

candidates.title: Hunter × Hunter
candidates.rationale: Its shifting structures and complex contests repeatedly challenge the conventions of its own adventure genre.

candidates.title: Ordinary Victories
candidates.rationale: An accessible cartoon surface supports sensitive, politically aware observations about precarious work, inheritance and emotional life.

candidates.title: Death Note
candidates.rationale: An exceptionally strong high-concept premise generates intricate contests over information, identity and moral authority.

candidates.title: Doom Patrol (Grant Morrison run)
candidates.creators_reported: Grant Morrison; Richard Case; John Nyberg and collaborators
candidates.rationale: Its surreal threats and outsider community use superhero strangeness to explore unstable bodies, identities and systems of control.

candidates.title: Attack on Titan
candidates.rationale: Its large structural reversals and relentless interrogation of collective violence outweigh uneven drawing and a divisive resolution.

candidates.title: Portugal
candidates.rationale: Fluid colour and drawing styles make a search for family history inseparable from a changing way of seeing.

candidates.title: BLAME!
candidates.rationale: Vast built environments and minimal explanation create an unusually powerful experience of scale, isolation and technological estrangement.

candidates.title: Monica
candidates.rationale: A sequence of shifting genres makes the search for personal origins unstable, ominous and formally absorbing.

candidates.title: Dorohedoro
candidates.rationale: Grotesque design, eccentric warmth and a dense mystery produce a remarkably individual fictional world.

candidates.title: Notes for a War Story
candidates.scope: Original Appunti per una storia di guerra.
candidates.rationale: Its deliberately unspecified conflict concentrates attention on vulnerability, social hierarchy and the seductions of violence.

candidates.title: Delicious in Dungeon
candidates.rationale: Its food-centred premise develops into an unusually coherent fantasy ecosystem and a rewarding exploration of desire and responsibility.

candidates.title: The Invisibles
candidates.creators_reported: Grant Morrison; Steve Yeowell; Jill Thompson; Phil Jimenez; Chris Weston and others
candidates.rationale: Ambitious, uneven and deeply inventive, it uses serial comics to test ideas about identity, freedom and constructed reality.

candidates.title: Witch Hat Atelier
candidates.rationale: Elegant page design and a thoughtful treatment of knowledge, exclusion and power give familiar apprenticeship fantasy unusual substance.

candidates.title: Blood of the Virgin
candidates.rationale: Its crowded professional and domestic world develops a searching account of artistic ambition, compromise and displacement.

candidates.title: Land of the Lustrous
candidates.rationale: Its austere design and radical character transformation turn a striking premise into an ambitious inquiry into selfhood and attachment.

candidates.title: Planetary
candidates.creators_reported: Warren Ellis; John Cassaday; Laura Martin
candidates.rationale: Elegant visual storytelling and a carefully unfolding mystery turn twentieth-century popular genres into an interconnected archaeology.

candidates.title: A Silent Voice
candidates.rationale: Its strongest passages examine the difficulty of accountability and communication with a visual vocabulary closely tied to perception.

candidates.title: Shubeik Lubeik / Your Wish Is My Command
candidates.genres: Urban fantasy; class; politics; mental health
candidates.scope: Complete original Arabic trilogy / collected English book.
candidates.rationale: Its commodified-wishes premise becomes a rich, visually inventive examination of unequal opportunity and individual longing.

candidates.title: The Climber
candidates.creators_reported: Shin'ichi Sakamoto; Yoshirō Nabeda initially; based on Jirō Nitta
candidates.rationale: Increasingly experimental imagery translates isolation and physical extremity into some of contemporary manga's most striking pages.

candidates.title: Transmetropolitan
candidates.rationale: A forceful, visually crowded satire whose best passages link political spectacle to reporting, class and civic responsibility.

candidates.title: Solanin
candidates.rationale: A compact, emotionally credible account of uncertainty, work and artistic aspiration after the reassuring structures of youth disappear.

candidates.title: The Property
candidates.rationale: Controlled character acting and layered conversations make an inheritance journey a nuanced account of family memory and competing motives.

candidates.title: My Lesbian Experience with Loneliness
candidates.manga_context: Autobiographical web manga; demographic not fixed
candidates.rationale: Its direct cartooning and refusal of tidy self-improvement narratives make private difficulty unusually communicable.

candidates.title: Preacher
candidates.scope: Main 66-issue narrative and connected original specials.
candidates.rationale: Its outrageous surface is anchored by memorable relationships and Dillon's exceptional ability to convey emotion through faces.

candidates.title: Pink
candidates.rationale: Brisk, deliberately dissonant storytelling connects consumer culture, emotional precarity and the performance of adult femininity.

candidates.title: Exit Wounds
candidates.rationale: An uncertain search becomes a perceptive study of intimacy, class and emotional distance in a politically charged everyday setting.

candidates.title: Helter Skelter
candidates.scope: Original narrative collected as one book.
candidates.rationale: An abrasive examination of beauty as labour, commodity and bodily risk, strengthened by Okazaki's distinctive visual voice.

candidates.title: Y: The Last Man
candidates.creators_reported: Brian K. Vaughan; Pia Guerra; José Marzán Jr. and collaborators
candidates.rationale: An accessible long-form adventure whose strongest asset is the changing emotional relationship between its travelling companions.

candidates.title: River's Edge
candidates.rationale: Its detached surface and sudden emotional shocks offer a bleak, influential portrait of young people living without reliable moral bearings.

candidates.title: Chicken with Plums
candidates.rationale: A compact, darkly comic narrative whose shifting recollections complicate a musician's apparently straightforward decision.

candidates.title: Chihayafuru
candidates.rationale: Makes a specialised competitive pursuit accessible through carefully developed rivalries, teamwork and personal growth.

candidates.title: Criminal
candidates.scope: Principal Criminal stories; separate creator projects excluded.
candidates.rationale: Its interlinked lives and assured atmosphere make inherited failure, loyalty and self-deception central to modern crime comics.

candidates.title: Basara
candidates.rationale: Its expansive cast and conflicted political romance give shōjo adventure substantial moral and emotional range.

candidates.title: Wrinkles
candidates.rationale: Clear cartooning and unsentimental companionship make institutional old age visible without reducing its characters to their illnesses.

candidates.title: Banana Fish
candidates.rationale: An influential fusion of crime thriller and intense emotional attachment, distinguished by its sustained dramatic momentum.

candidates.title: Gotham Central
candidates.creators_reported: Ed Brubaker; Greg Rucka; Michael Lark; Stefano Gaudiano and collaborators
candidates.rationale: A convincing ensemble procedural whose encounters with superhero spectacle retain the vulnerability and limited power of ordinary people.

candidates.title: Sailor Moon
candidates.scope: Original manga, including its principal story arcs.
candidates.rationale: Its lasting importance lies in the imaginative and cultural reach of its female-led magical adventure and romantic cosmology.

candidates.title: The House
candidates.rationale: Objects, work and physical space carry the emotional history of a family with exceptional economy.

candidates.title: Cardcaptor Sakura
candidates.scope: Original twelve-volume story; Clear Card excluded.
candidates.rationale: Graceful page design and a comparatively generous emotional world make it a particularly accomplished magical-girl manga.

candidates.title: Parker (Darwyn Cooke adaptations)
candidates.creators_reported: Darwyn Cooke; based on Richard Stark
candidates.rationale: Design, restrained colour and visual pacing translate hard-boiled prose into exceptionally assured crime comics.

candidates.title: Princess Knight
candidates.scope: Tezuka's Princess Knight, with the 1963–1966 version as the main reading text.
candidates.rationale: Historically crucial to shōjo's development, its theatrical adventure and conflicted gender roles remain valuable to understanding the form.

candidates.title: Paracuellos
candidates.rationale: Its incisive cartooning records the cruelty and survival strategies of institutionalised children with fierce personal authority.

candidates.title: Maison Ikkoku
candidates.rationale: A beautifully sustained ensemble comedy whose slow emotional development gives its eventual payoffs unusual weight.

candidates.title: Usagi Yojimbo
candidates.rationale: Decades of lucid, humane storytelling balance self-contained adventures with a convincingly accumulating world and supporting cast.

candidates.title: Honey and Clover
candidates.rationale: Combines lively comedy with a perceptive account of unrequited love, artistic insecurity and the transition into adult life.

candidates.title: The Art of Flying
candidates.scope: Original El arte de volar; companion books excluded.
candidates.rationale: An individual life becomes an unsparing account of historical defeat, compromised hopes and the limits of personal freedom.

candidates.title: Touch
candidates.rationale: Its pauses, economical dialogue and emotional restraint show how much a sports-romance manga can accomplish through understatement.

candidates.title: Scott Pilgrim
candidates.rationale: Its synthesis of game logic, manga influence and messy personal development creates a distinctive comic account of young adulthood.

candidates.title: Emma
candidates.scope: Main romance and original supplementary stories.
candidates.rationale: Patient drawing and close attention to manners and labour lend a restrained cross-class romance unusual texture.

candidates.title: Spirou and Fantasio (Franquin run)
candidates.creators_reported: André Franquin; collaborators including Greg and Jidéhem
candidates.rationale: Energetic character acting, imaginative machines and strong adventure construction helped define the modern Franco-Belgian comic album.

candidates.title: The Color of Earth
candidates.genres: Coming of age; family; rural life
candidates.rationale: Lyrical environmental imagery and an intimate mother–daughter relationship give its account of growing up a distinctive voice.

candidates.title: Stray Bullets
candidates.rationale: Its dislocated chronology and ordinary settings make violence feel unpredictable, intimate and consequential.

candidates.title: Uncomfortably Happily
candidates.rationale: Its gently comic treatment of artistic work and domestic anxiety complicates the fantasy of escaping the city for a simpler life.

candidates.title: Lucky Luke (Morris–Goscinny albums)
candidates.rationale: Graphic economy and expertly organised gags turn Western conventions and historical figures into remarkably durable comic adventures.

candidates.title: The Waiting
candidates.rationale: A restrained, deeply humane narrative about separation and the passage of time, built around the intimate costs of divided history.

candidates.title: Sin City
candidates.rationale: Extremely bold black-and-white design makes it an important visual achievement, even where its gender politics and plotting narrow its appeal.

candidates.title: The Ravages of Time
candidates.rationale: An ambitious strategic reworking of the Three Kingdoms tradition, valued for intricate political conflict and sustained visual intensity.

candidates.title: Thorgal (Van Hamme–Rosiński cycle)
candidates.scope: Original principal creators' cycle, through The Sacrifice.
candidates.rationale: Its strongest stories combine mythic adventure with a persistent desire for family and peace rather than conquest.

candidates.title: Old Master Q
candidates.creators_reported: Alfonso Wong (Wong Chak); classic original strip corpus
candidates.rationale: An essential Hong Kong popular-comics tradition whose expressive physical comedy and urban observations travel readily across language barriers.

candidates.title: Fables (original 150-issue cycle)
candidates.creators_reported: Bill Willingham; Mark Buckingham; Steve Leialoha and collaborators
candidates.rationale: Its strongest stretches turn familiar characters into a lively, evolving community with sustained political and emotional stakes.

candidates.title: Sanmao
candidates.scope: Zhang Leping's classic strips, especially the orphan cycle.
candidates.rationale: Its vulnerable child protagonist and often wordless storytelling give social criticism an enduring visual immediacy.

candidates.title: The Quest for the Time-Bird
candidates.rationale: Expressive drawing and a tightly bounded quest give familiar fantasy materials emotional sharpness and a memorable tragic shape.

candidates.title: Bhimayana
candidates.creators_reported: Durgabai Vyam; Subhash Vyam; Srividya Natarajan; S. Anand
candidates.genres: Caste; biography; social justice; Gond art
candidates.rationale: Its Gond visual vocabulary challenges familiar panel conventions while connecting Ambedkar's experience to continuing structures of exclusion.

candidates.title: The Walking Dead
candidates.creators_reported: Robert Kirkman; Tony Moore; Charlie Adlard
candidates.rationale: Its long duration lets a survival premise develop into an unusually sustained examination of social order and its human costs.

candidates.title: Munnu: A Boy from Kashmir
candidates.rationale: Distinctive animal representation and local detail connect artistic coming of age with life under prolonged political violence.

candidates.title: Valérian and Laureline
candidates.rationale: Its visual inventions and often sceptical politics helped expand the imaginative repertoire of European space adventure.

candidates.title: Batman: The Killing Joke
candidates.creators_reported: Alan Moore; Brian Bolland; John Higgins
candidates.scope: Original one-shot; recoloured editions change its visual treatment.
candidates.rationale: Bolland's exact drawing and the circular construction sustain its canonical position, while its treatment of Barbara Gordon significantly qualifies that achievement.

candidates.title: The Rabbi's Cat
candidates.rationale: Loose, expressive drawing and a questioning animal narrator create an unusually lively conversation about faith, identity and coexistence.

candidates.title: Invincible
candidates.creators_reported: Robert Kirkman; Cory Walker; Ryan Ottley
candidates.rationale: A sustained, self-contained superhero life that combines genre reinvention with long-running personal and family consequences.

candidates.title: Dungeon
candidates.creators_reported: Joann Sfar; Lewis Trondheim; numerous artists
candidates.scope: Main linked Dungeon cycles; strongest emphasis on early Zenith and Twilight.
candidates.rationale: Its changing tones and historical layers transform fantasy parody into an expansive, emotionally consequential world.

candidates.title: Miracleman (Alan Moore cycle)
candidates.creators_reported: Alan Moore; Garry Leach; Alan Davis; Chuck Austen; Rick Veitch; John Totleben
candidates.scope: Moore's three-book cycle; Neil Gaiman continuation excluded.
candidates.rationale: A foundational revision of superhero power whose changing visual approaches culminate in an unsettling political vision.

candidates.title: Aâma
candidates.rationale: Organic visual invention and a troubled family relationship make speculative transformation feel psychologically intimate.

candidates.title: The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen (first two volumes)
candidates.scope: Original Volumes I and II; later cycles excluded.
candidates.rationale: Dense literary play and distinctive grotesque drawing produce an inventive, sharply bounded adventure across Victorian popular fiction.

candidates.title: On a Sunbeam
candidates.rationale: Expansive visual environments and intimate relationships create a distinctive fusion of space fantasy and emotional coming of age.

candidates.title: The Ballad of Halo Jones
candidates.scope: The three completed books; planned continuation unwritten.
candidates.rationale: Its ordinary heroine and attention to social systems give a partial science-fiction epic unusual emotional and political resonance.

candidates.title: Sabrina
candidates.rationale: Its flat, controlled visual language creates a chilling account of private grief inside a culture of speculation and mediated suspicion.

candidates.title: Judge Dredd: America
candidates.rationale: A compact and devastating examination of citizenship, resistance and state violence within the Dredd setting.

candidates.title: Rusty Brown
candidates.scope: Published 2019 volume; not a claim about an uncompleted larger design.
candidates.rationale: Its individual lives and recursive structures show Ware's exceptional ability to turn minute visual choices into psychological depth.

candidates.title: Nemesis the Warlock
candidates.creators_reported: Pat Mills; Kevin O'Neill; Bryan Talbot and others
candidates.rationale: Grotesque visual invention and uncompromising satire make it one of British weekly comics' most distinctive long adventures.

candidates.title: David Boring
candidates.rationale: A deliberately opaque mixture of melodrama and estrangement, rewarding readers who attend to its visual patterns and unstable tone.

candidates.title: The Adventures of Luther Arkwright
candidates.rationale: Its dense, nonlinear construction demonstrates the ambitious formal possibilities of British adult adventure comics.

candidates.title: Ice Haven
candidates.rationale: Its collection of contrasting strip styles creates a compact, sharply controlled portrait of a community and its private obsessions.

candidates.title: Gemma Bovery
candidates.rationale: A sophisticated mixture of prose and pictures exposes the dangers of interpreting real people through a favourite literary plot.

candidates.title: Tamara Drewe
candidates.rationale: Exceptionally acute character observation and a supple text-image relationship make its literary milieu both funny and unsettling.

candidates.title: Ethel & Ernest
candidates.rationale: Economical domestic scenes turn an ordinary marriage into a moving portrait of social change and a son's remembrance.

candidates.title: When the Wind Blows
candidates.rationale: The collision of reassuring household habits with incomprehensible catastrophe makes its antiwar argument extraordinarily affecting.

candidates.title: Alice in Sunderland
candidates.rationale: Its exuberant mixture of documentary material, performance and graphic styles gives local history an unusually expansive comics form.

candidates.title: Can't We Talk about Something More Pleasant?
candidates.rationale: Anxiety, irritation and love coexist in a candid account whose visual humour makes difficult family experience sharply recognisable.

candidates.title: My New York Diary
candidates.scope: The collected diary narrative; Dirty Plotte is not separately ranked.
candidates.rationale: Dense, unruly drawing gives psychological and domestic discomfort an unmistakably personal visual presence.

candidates.title: Binky Brown Meets the Holy Virgin Mary
candidates.rationale: Historically pivotal to autobiographical comics, it turns private compulsions into an inventive and startlingly explicit visual system.

candidates.title: One! Hundred! Demons!
candidates.rationale: Its apparent spontaneity conceals a finely developed account of memory, shame and the imaginative resources of childhood.

candidates.title: Dykes to Watch Out For
candidates.rationale: A sustained ensemble portrait whose domestic arguments and political differences accumulate into a rich record of community life.

candidates.title: Gods' Man
candidates.rationale: Its dramatic image sequences established a major American precedent for extended narrative told through pictures alone.

candidates.title: Passionate Journey
candidates.rationale: A foundational European wordless narrative whose emotional and social range demonstrates the power of sequential images without dialogue.

candidates.title: The Cage
candidates.rationale: An exacting experiment in spaces, objects and unstable narration, extending graphic storytelling beyond conventional character-driven plots.

candidates.title: Big Questions
candidates.rationale: Its apparently simple birds and expansive silences support a searching, often funny inquiry into belief and meaning.

candidates.title: The Sky Is Blue with a Single Cloud
candidates.scope: English collection of Tsurita's selected stories.
candidates.rationale: Its visual and tonal variety recovers an important alternative-manga voice whose experiments complicate an overly male account of the tradition.

candidates.title: The Green Hand and Other Stories
candidates.scope: The collected stories; Zha scripted The Green Hand.
candidates.rationale: Its vivid transformations and distinctive colour work demonstrate an imaginative tradition insufficiently represented by conventional adventure and superhero canons.

candidates.title: Finder
candidates.rationale: Its layered societies and attention to custom, kinship and marginality make world-building itself a form of characterisation.

candidates.title: The Nao of Brown
candidates.rationale: Sensitive watercolour drawing and a carefully observed London setting give intrusive thoughts and ordinary relationships a distinctive emotional texture.

candidates.title: The Many Deaths of Laila Starr
candidates.creators_reported: Ram V; Filipe Andrade; Inês Amaro
candidates.rationale: A compact, visually exuberant meditation on death whose changing human encounters give an abstract premise emotional immediacy.
